title: Bad Listing Photos Are Costing You Viewings
description: Buyers scroll past bad photos in two seconds. Fix, resize and watermark your listing shots in a browser — then let AI show what the rooms could become.
excerpt: The first photo decides. Blurry files and HEIC uploads are how listings die quietly.
content:
Buyers decide on a listing in seconds. Bad photos close the tab before anyone reads the description. And most real estate photos aren't bad because of the room — they're bad because of the file.

## The file is the problem

Your phone shoots HEIC. The portal wants JPG. The photo is 8 MB and the portal cuts it at 4. None of that has anything to do with how the room looks. [FileTools](https://filetools.eu) converts HEIC to JPG, resizes images to portal limits and compresses the result — right in the browser, no account, no install.

Do it in this order: convert, resize, compress. Convert first, because resizing a HEIC invites weird results. Compress last, because resizing already shrank the file and a second squeeze kills quality.

## One photo, three jobs

The wide shot goes on the portal. A compressed copy goes into the WhatsApp group with serious buyers. A watermarked version stops other agents from reusing your pictures on their listings. [FileTools](https://filetools.eu) does all three in one tab.

## Sell the potential, not the problems

Empty rooms and dated kitchens invite lowball offers. Feed the photo into [RoomFlip](https://roomflip.io) and let the AI restyle it — modern sofa, new floor, better light. You get a realistic after-render in seconds. List it next to the original and buyers stop guessing what the room could become. That's the difference between a viewing and a skip.

## Batch the boring part

Twenty photos, one by one, wastes an afternoon. Upload the folder, convert and resize everything at once. Files never leave your machine — pictures of someone's future home don't belong on a random server.

Stop losing viewings to bad files. Convert, resize, restyle, list.
